opportunities.title: Junior Scientist Conference Grants

deadlines.raw: 1st day of February, April, June, August, October and December

amount.raw: Grants up to £200 for Scheme (A), up to £500 for Scheme (B), up to £300 for Scheme (C).

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Eligibility varies by scheme: Scheme (A) is open to undergraduate, Master’s and PhD student members and to postdoctoral scientist members within six years of their PhD viva. Schemes (B) & (C) are open to PhD student and postdoctoral scientist members within six years of their PhD viva. Schemes (B) & (C) are open to members with a UK base wishing to attend conferences outside of the UK and to non-UK-based members wishing to attend a conference in the UK.
opportunities.summary: Supports attendance at conferences on research in Genetics.

opportunities.title: Training Grant
opportunities.eligibility_summary: All members of the Genetics Society can apply, as long as you are studying or working in the UK, or the course you wish to attend is being held in the UK. Students can apply as soon as they become Society members. Others should be a Society member for at least one year.
opportunities.summary: Grants of up to £1,200 to enable members to attend formal short training courses, or a collaborative visit to another laboratory to train in specific genetic/genomic techniques.

opportunities.title: Heredity Fieldwork Grant
opportunities.eligibility_summary: All members of the Genetics Society can apply, as long as you are studying or working in the UK, or you intend to carry out your fieldwork in the UK. Students can apply as soon as they become Society members. Others should be a Society member for at least one year.
opportunities.summary: Supports travel and accommodation costs associated with a field-based genetic research project.

opportunities.title: Summer Studentship

amount.raw: £425/week allowance for up to 8 weeks, up to £750 to cover host laboratory expenses.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: The Summer Studentship scheme is open to all undergraduate students, except those in their first or final year. The project must be based at a UK university.
opportunities.summary: Supports undergraduate students to gain experience in any area of genetics by doing a research project during the summer holiday prior to the final year of their degree.

opportunities.title: Communicating Your Science Workshop

amount.raw: The Genetics Society will cover travel (within the UK only), accommodation and meals for successful applicants.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: The course is open to PhD student and postdoctoral researcher Society members working in genetics and related areas.
opportunities.summary: A workshop to help participants explore and develop their communication skills in science.

opportunities.title: Carer’s Award
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Any member can apply, regardless of age of person they are caring for.
opportunities.summary: An award of (up to) £60/day to be used as you think will best support your attendance.

opportunities.title: One-off Meeting

amount.raw: Several levels of sponsorship are possible. We can sponsor a specific Genetics Society lecture for a few hundred pounds or a Genetics Society session for up to about £1,000. As major sponsor of an entire meeting we can potentially sponsor several thousand pounds but the costs need to be well justified.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Members may apply at any time of the year and we encourage members to submit at least three months in advance of their event to allow the application to be reviewed.
opportunities.summary: Sponsorship of genetic themed meetings not organised directly by the Genetics Society.

opportunities.title: Public Engagement
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Grants of up to £1,000 are available to members of the Genetics Society to support public engagement activities related to genetics.
opportunities.summary: Supports public engagement activities related to genetics.

opportunities.title: New Special Interest Group
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applications to become a new Special Interest Group should be submitted at least three months before the date of the first meeting and include a funding proposal.
opportunities.summary: Sponsorship of research meetings on particular themes.
